title: Why agent evaluations should be treated as production-risk systems
friendlyTitle: Testing an AI agent can change real systems
summary: A new incident-grounded paper argues that agent evaluations stop being passive measurements once models receive shells, browsers, credentials, networks, and mutation-capable tools. It proposes six independent boundaries covering execution, networks, identity, external effects, evaluation integrity, and evidence and response.
friendlySummary: A paper explains that an AI test is not harmless when the agent can use a computer, network, browser, or real login details. It suggests six separate safety boundaries for these tests.
whyItMatters: Teams testing capable agents can cause real damage even when the intended task is only a benchmark. Treating evaluation workloads like hostile production code—with default-deny networking, scoped credentials, isolated graders, and off-box logs—reduces the blast radius when an agent explores beyond the expected path.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A benchmark can become a real security incident if the test environment is weak. Teams should isolate agents, limit their access, and keep reliable records of every action.
